Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

confidence noun

trust that someone or something will not fail

also confident, be confident that, have confidence in, I’m confident that, I’m sure it will be fine

classical

Ter. Haut. 160: Salvum affutūrum esse hīc cōnfīdō propediem.
Cic. Att. 12.23.3: rēctē esse cōnfīdō
Traupman 150

cōnfīdō, cōnfīdere, cōnfīsus sum

verb, third conjugation, semi-deponent: with an accusative and infinitive (“I’m confident that”), or with the dative or ablative (“trust in”)

be confident (that), trust

In speech Latin says the verb: cōnfīdō is a firm hope, stronger than spērō (Cic. Att. 6.9.1, Lewis & Short). For relying on someone, see depend.

Other words

  • fīdūcia, fīdūciae f. — confidence, trust, reliance

    noun, first declension: with the genitive of what one trusts · also used · classical · Caes. BC 2.37.1 (Lewis & Short): tantam habēbat suārum rērum fīdūciam; Traupman 150

    The noun: trust in a person, a thing or a plan; fīdūcia suī is self-confidence (see self-confidence). In law it is also a pledge held in trust (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • Salvum affutūrum esse hīc cōnfīdō propediem.

    I’m confident he’ll be back here safe and sound any day now.Ter. Haut. 160

  • dē Atticā molestum, sed quoniam leviter, rēctē esse cōnfīdō.

    Too bad about Attica, but since it’s mild, I’m confident she’ll be fine.Cic. Att. 12.23.3

  • quī reliquiās hujus bellī oppresserit, eum tōtīus bellī cōnfectōrem fore; quem tē et optō esse et cōnfīdō futūrum.

    whoever crushes what is left of this war will be the one who ends the whole war; and that is what I hope you are, and am confident you will be.Cic. Fam. 10.20.3

See also self-confidence, depend, hope, positive.
